analysis.title: Komatsu (6301.T): 2Q Follow-up: Maintain bullish stance, focus on improvement from FY3/28
key_insights: Komatsu's share price has underperformed the machinery sector since the 2Q results because operating profit and the new full-year guidance missed market expectations, largely on one-off costs. GS says the disappointment stems mainly from temporary factors.

2Q operating profit missed market consensus and GS estimates by about ¥15-20 bn. Drivers: Thailand flood response and overseas supplier quality costs (about ¥5 bn vs consensus), timing of tariff refunds on the P&L (about ¥5-10 bn), and a sales/shipment timing mismatch for mining machinery bound for Australia (low single-digit ¥ bn).

Komatsu estimates the yoy profit drag from these factors at over ¥11 bn in 1H and just under ¥20 bn for the full year. Positive operating leverage and mix effects were not large enough to offset them.

North American general construction machinery sales are strong, but growth in high-margin mining machinery and components is relatively weak. The profit mix improvement GS had expected has not yet materialized.
GS expects margins to improve heading into FY3/28, driven by a bottoming of Asian coal-mine machinery demand and a recovery in the components/services sales mix.
Mining machinery demand is tracking above Komatsu's initial expectations, with strong inquiries from copper mines (mainly South America) and gold mines (mainly Africa).

Indonesian coal mine leading indicators are starting to bottom out. The idle rate fell from about 20% at the end of 1Q to 12-13% in September. Permitting uncertainty remains, and Komatsu stays cautious on calendar 2027 coal volumes, but the yoy hurdle is lowering.
Komatsu's 2H outlook for Asia mining machinery sales (AeCJ) assumes a yoy turnaround and continued growth. GS sees ample scope for improvement into FY3/28 because this is a highly profitable segment.
Komatsu estimates North American construction machinery demand rose 15% yoy in 1H, with rental demand up 55%. AI and data center investment is cited as a driver.

Customers prioritizing early construction starts are favoring rentals over purchases. Komatsu is capturing this through inventory restocking for dealer rent-to-sell. GS sees some signs of slowing non-residential demand but few signs of significant deterioration, and views Komatsu's cautious assumptions as conservative.

CAT also reported dealer rental fleet loading contributing significantly to sales to users growth in Construction Industries. North American STU in 3Q grew 27% yoy. Booking timing differs between CAT's DORF and Komatsu's rent-to-sell data, so the two are hard to compare directly. The sustainability of rental demand needs monitoring.

GS cuts its FY3/27 operating profit estimate by 1% to ¥625 bn (from ¥630 bn) on a larger mix impact. FY3/28 operating profit stays at ¥700 bn and FY3/29 at ¥760 bn. GS reiterates Buy with a 12-month target price of ¥9,000, 44.9% above the ¥6,213 close on 2 Nov 2026.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy on Komatsu (6301.T) with an unchanged ¥9,000 target. It sees the 2Q profit miss as temporary and expects profit growth from FY3/28 on mix improvement. Komatsu has no US listing, so the ticker is left empty.

sector_views.rationale: North American construction demand, helped by data centers and rentals, is strong. Mining demand for copper and gold is above Komatsu's initial expectations, and Indonesian coal demand is starting to bottom.

earnings_insights: Komatsu 2Q FY3/27 (reported): operating profit missed market consensus and GS estimates by about ¥15-20 bn, mostly on temporary factors (Thailand flood and supplier quality costs, tariff refund timing, Australia mining shipment timing).
GS FY3/27E operating profit is now ¥625.0 bn (GS estimate), down from ¥630.0 bn. The company-compiled consensus (CoE) is ¥585.0 bn. FY3/26 actual operating profit was ¥567.3 bn.
GS estimates FY3/27E EPS at ¥460.6 (old ¥464.5). FY3/28E EPS is ¥524.9 and FY3/29E is ¥579.4, both unchanged. FY3/26 EPS was ¥413.9.
Quarterly EPS (GS table): ¥107.2 for 6/26 and ¥107.9 for 9/26, then GS estimates of ¥116.6 for 12/26E and ¥129.0 for 3/27E.
GS FY3/27E revenue is ¥4,533.7 bn, FY3/28E is ¥4,818.9 bn and FY3/29E is ¥5,121.6 bn, against FY3/26 revenue of ¥4,132.8 bn.
Komatsu expects the yoy profit drag from the temporary factors at over ¥11 bn in 1H and just under ¥20 bn for the full year.

trade_ideas.description: Buy Komatsu (6301.T) with a 12-month target price of ¥9,000
trade_ideas.rationale: GS expects profit growth from FY3/28 as mining and components mix recovers and North American construction demand stays strong.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker mining machinery demand or lower utilization from falling commodity prices or lower mining capex. A slowdown in North American non-residential and data center construction if US rates stay elevated. A pullback in share buybacks.

risk_factors: Weaker-than-expected mining machinery demand and lower production utilization from lower commodity prices or mining capex.
A slowdown in North American non-residential and data center construction if US interest rates stay elevated for longer than expected.
A change in capital allocation policy, such as a pullback in share buybacks, which could push Komatsu's valuation discount back toward its historical average.
Uncertainty over Indonesian coal production permits and volumes for calendar 2027.
Sustainability of North American rental demand, where competitors such as CAT are also expanding.
geopolitical: Indonesia's government coal production permits remain uncertain, which affects Komatsu's coal mining machinery demand.
Tariff refunds are being recognized on Komatsu's P&L, and the timing of that recognition contributed to the 2Q profit miss.

tension_points.bull_case: GS says the 2Q miss reflects one-off costs and timing mismatches. It expects mix to improve and profit to grow from FY3/28 as Asian coal mining and components/services recover, with FY3/28 operating profit at ¥700 bn.
tension_points.bear_case: High-margin mining machinery and components growth is relatively weak, the expected mix improvement has not materialized, and FY3/27 mix drag is larger than GS assumed. North American rental demand may be less durable than it looks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weaker mining machinery demand or lower utilization from falling commodity prices or mining capex, or a slowdown in North American non-residential and data center construction.

theme_stances.key_argument: The 2Q miss owes mainly to temporary factors, and mix improvement should lift profit growth from FY3/28.
theme_stances.evidence: outlook for profit growth heading into FY3/28 is actually opening up

theme_stances.key_argument: Data center investment is driving North American construction demand, with customers favoring rentals, and Komatsu's cautious assumptions look conservative.
theme_stances.evidence: we view its assumptions as conservative
